strengths: The paper addresses a useful problem: improving minority-class accuracy while retaining previously learned classes and learning representations of future classes. Combining persistent class prototypes with an adaptable cluster-assignment model has practical potential for continual segmentation.

The evaluation covers three datasets, multiple incremental schedules, and both DeepLab-V3 and SegFormer. Table 5 reports consistent improvements over FairCL: 37.9 versus 37.0 mIoU on ADE20K 100-50 and 36.4 versus 34.7 on 100-10 with DeepLab-V3; the corresponding Transformer improvements are larger.

Table 1 provides concrete evidence of improved class balance. On ADE20K 100-50, the fairness loss increases minority-class mIoU from 26.4 to 30.8 while improving majority-class mIoU from 51.5 to 52.1. The gap between the groups consequently decreases from 25.1 to 21.3 points.

The component and sensitivity studies are substantial, covering loss terms, grammar adaptation, scaling factor, cluster margin, neighborhood size, and backbone. The framework diagrams, training algorithm, and appendix implementation details help communicate the overall approach.
weaknesses: The central fairness explanation is not established by Propositions 1–2. The quantity ℓ_i is a probability normalized over features; its optimum of 1/L reflects normalization and does not establish cluster compactness. Duplicating identical features changes this probability without changing their geometry. Consequently, reducing differences between these probabilities across classes does not prove the claimed improvement in minority-cluster compactness or prediction fairness. This is a substantive gap in the principal theoretical contribution.

The stated optimization contains consequential ambiguities. Proposition 2 requires the transition vector v to participate in the normalization, but Eq. (4) retains the denominator defined over feature representations. Under that stated feature-only denominator, the loss is unbounded below as v·c increases. Separately, Eq. (8) optimizes θ_t while its regularizer depends only on centers described as frozen or updated by momentum; no differentiable dependence or separate center optimization explains the regularizer's improvements in Table 4. These issues prevent reconciling the reported results with the specified objective.

Appendix Section 4 does not establish the claimed relationship to knowledge distillation. It applies a triangle inequality to an abstract metric and then identifies the resulting distance with the contrastive loss without demonstrating that equivalence. The subsequent Big-O argument does not show that minimizing the proposed objective preserves previous predictions.

The unknown-class ablation does not isolate the attention model's contribution. Section 4.2 states that removing visual grammar also switches to a single unknown cluster and nearest-cluster assignment. A comparison retaining the same multiple DBSCAN clusters and changing only the assignment model is absent. Figure 6 offers qualitative support, but no quantitative unknown-cluster assignment evaluation resolves this confounding. Since the attention architecture follows Clusformer [35], establishing the additional contribution of this adaptation is particularly important.

The fairness evaluation supports improved group averages but leaves the broader claim insufficiently characterized. The Major/Minor partition is not precisely specified, and these averages can conceal poorly performing individual classes. Comparisons against FairCL do not report the same fairness breakdown. Matched comparisons with simpler class-balancing objectives or the cited parametric/balanced contrastive approaches would also help establish the distinctive value of the proposed loss.

Important reproducibility details remain unspecified, including DBSCAN parameters, how unknown pixels are selected from background containing both old and future classes, resolution of competing cluster assignments, and the visual-grammar pretraining and training schedules. No runtime or memory measurements substantiate the efficiency claim despite the additional 12-layer attention model and clustering pipeline. The unresolved objective definitions and component attribution, together with the unsupported central theoretical explanation, determine the weak-reject recommendation despite the worthwhile empirical gains.
